guard: cotal_inbox clears only the messages it actually returned, and one response stays inside a receivable window with first-party mail ahead of replayed history
why: The defect this guards is a composition, so the kills are split along its parts rather than aimed
at one line. K2 restores the drain-the-whole-scope order, K3 removes mail-before-replay, K4 and K7
let peek clear on each path, K5 silences the held-note, K6 acks read-only recall, K11 unbounds the
note, K12 gives stuck mail the waiting mail's promise, K14 unbounds the recall warning, K15 gives a
peeking caller a promise peek cannot keep, and K16 re-serves recall from the same frontier forever.
K17 through K20 are the recall walk, which this change created and therefore owns. A lane walked
by a single mark can fail in four ways and each has a mutation: comparing times alone strands a
tie, a mark that forgets its id repeats one, stepping over a gap re-serves everything behind it,
and a mark that follows the last item shown strands whatever the gap held. The invariant they
guard together is total progress: every fresh item eventually delivered, and nothing delivered
twice, on inputs including a same-millisecond pair too large to share one window.
K1, K8, K9 and K10 are the class guard and its edges. Three escapes were found here in sequence,
each the same defect one level further out: an oversized item shown alone, then the head and note
riding outside the budget, then the focus warning appended after the window was filled. Every one
was a writer to the response body the arithmetic did not know about, so the arithmetic was replaced
by assembling the reply and measuring it. K1 disables that measurement, K8 makes an undeliverable
item block the queue, K9 empties the stuck class, and K10 hides a buffer that could deliver nothing.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed. The suite imports the agent and the tool specs
by RELATIVE SOURCE PATH (../src/agent.js, ../src/tool-specs.js), so the bytes mutated are the
bytes graded: no dist in the path and no build in the command. Its only package-name import is
`type` from @cotal-ai/core, erased at compile time and carrying no behaviour.
NOT PROVED HERE, named rather than implied. The 48,000-character budget is a judgement, not a
measurement of any one host's cap: no mutation can show it is the RIGHT number, only that a bound
is enforced and that what falls outside it is kept. An earlier mutation that subtracted the recall
warning from the budget a second time SURVIVED and the code it targeted was deleted rather than
kept: with the reply assembled and measured, no input could tell the two versions apart.
A SECOND SURVIVOR, resolved the same way as the first. A mutation on a walk that recomputed the
mark over the delivered prefix SURVIVED: the ordered lane already stops at its first gap, so the
last recall item shown IS the end of the prefix and no input could tell the two versions apart.
The walk was deleted rather than the test weakened, and the mark is the last item shown.

mutations.name: K1 the finished response is never measured, only estimated
mutations.expectRed: the head line and the held-note are inside the budget, not outside it
mutations.cell: the head line and the held-note are inside the budget, not outside it
mutations.note: THE CLASS GUARD. Three escapes were found here, each a writer to the response body that the arithmetic did not know about. This loop is what replaced the arithmetic: it measures the finished string and gives back trailing items until the real text fits. Disable it and the estimate alone decides again, which is where every one of those escapes lived. The cell that notices first is the near-boundary one: with the measurement disabled the estimate is all that is left, and the estimate is exactly what does not know about the framing.

mutations.name: K2 clear the whole scope up front, the order the defect was written in
mutations.expectRed: what did not fit was NOT consumed: the buffer still holds the rest
mutations.cell: what did not fit was NOT consumed: the buffer still holds the rest
mutations.note: The plausible authoring error rather than a contrived one: draining the scope is what the tool did before, and with a window in place it reads as a harmless simplification.

mutations.name: K3 rank every item the same - receive order alone decides the window
mutations.expectRed: the first response is mail, not backfill: DMs occupy the window ahead of replayed history
mutations.cell: the first response is mail, not backfill: DMs occupy the window ahead of replayed history
mutations.note: Without the rank a DM behind a replay waits for as many calls as the replay takes; the loss is gone but the mail is still last.

mutations.name: K4 peek clears what it shows
mutations.note: peek is the documented workaround for this very defect, so a peek that clears is the worst possible regression here.

mutations.name: K5 the response stops saying what it is holding back
mutations.expectRed: ...and it says what it is holding back
mutations.cell: ...and it says what it is holding back
mutations.note: Held mail nobody is told about is mail nobody calls back for - the loss becomes a silent delay instead.

mutations.name: K6 the focus drain acks every id in the reply, recall included
mutations.expectRed: focus: a recall id was NOT marked handled
mutations.cell: focus: a recall id was NOT marked handled, so a later live copy of it still buffers
mutations.note: The filter reads like defensive noise: the reply carries both lanes, so acking 'what the reply carried' is the obvious simplification. It is not - drainInboxIds marks an absent id HANDLED, so a later live copy of that channel message is dropped as a duplicate, and the read loses mail it never owned.

mutations.name: K7 the focus drain stops honouring peek
mutations.cell: focus + peek: the buffered lane is NOT cleared
mutations.expectRed: focus + peek: the buffered lane is NOT cleared
mutations.note: K4 covers the same slip on the ordinary path only. Without this one a focus reply could clear while peeking, and peek is the workaround this whole change exists to retire, so it has to hold on both paths.

mutations.name: K8 one message too large for any response blocks the queue behind it
mutations.cell: ordinary mail is delivered past an item that can never fit
mutations.expectRed: ordinary mail is delivered past an item that can never fit
mutations.note: The fill stops at the first item too large instead of stepping over it, so one message nobody can deliver blocks every message behind it. That is the wedge the show-alone escape was invented to avoid, arriving through the other door. Expressed here as the ordered lane's rule leaking onto the free lane, which is the plausible way it would be written.

mutations.name: K9 nothing is ever classified as too large to deliver
mutations.cell: ...and the reply names it rather than leaving it silently stuck
mutations.expectRed: ...and the reply names it rather than leaving it silently stuck
mutations.note: Stuck means no response could carry this message. Measure it against a budget nothing can exceed and the class becomes empty: the message is still held, correctly, but the reply calls it ordinary backlog and tells the caller to call again for it forever.

mutations.name: K10 nothing shown is reported as an empty inbox, whatever is held
mutations.find: else if (held.length) parts.push(`Nothing could be delivered in this response.${heldNote(held, peek, stuck)}`);
mutations.replace: else if (false) parts.push(`Nothing could be delivered in this response.${heldNote(held, peek, stuck)}`);
mutations.cell: ...and the reply names it rather than leaving it silently stuck
mutations.expectRed: ...and the reply names it rather than leaving it silently stuck
mutations.note: An inbox that says it is empty while holding mail it cannot deliver is the silent version of the same loss: nobody calls back for what they were told is not there. The cell that notices first is the oversized-item cell, because a single oversized message is exactly the case where nothing can be shown; the later empty-inbox cell asserts the same guard from the other side. mutations.name: K11 the note names every oversized message instead of a few
mutations.cell: twelve undeliverable messages do not produce twelve lines of metadata
mutations.expectRed: twelve undeliverable messages do not produce twelve lines of metadata
mutations.note: The obvious authoring choice, and the one the second lens flagged before it existed: naming them all is more informative per message and unbounded in aggregate, so a steady stream of oversized mail overflows the reply with metadata about mail it cannot carry.

mutations.name: K12 the stuck note borrows the waiting note's promise
mutations.find: buffered and uncleared, and calling again will not produce ${stuck.length === 1 ? "it" : "them"}.`,
mutations.replace: buffered and uncleared. Call cotal_inbox again for the next batch.`,
mutations.cell: ...and it does not promise that calling again will deliver them
mutations.expectRed: ...and it does not promise that calling again will deliver them
mutations.note: A queue that looks like it is moving when it is not. The caller keeps calling, the same messages keep not arriving, and nothing in the reply says why.

mutations.name: K14 the recall warning names every dropped channel
mutations.cell: ...and the warning is bounded rather than naming all eighty channels
mutations.expectRed: ...and the warning is bounded rather than naming all eighty channels
mutations.note: A caller with many silenced or expired channels is exactly the caller who gets a long list, so an unbounded list is not a rare case: it is the case. With the reply now assembled and measured, an unbounded warning no longer breaks the bound; it eats the window instead, giving back real messages to make room for channel names, which is why the boundedness assertion is the one that catches it.

mutations.name: K15 the held note gives a peeking caller the destructive read's promise
mutations.replace: const next = "Call cotal_inbox again for the next batch.";
mutations.cell: a peek that holds mail does not promise a next batch it cannot deliver
mutations.expectRed: a peek that holds mail does not promise a next batch it cannot deliver
mutations.note: Peek clears nothing, so the next call returns the same window. An obedient caller told to call again loops on it forever, which the first lens measured as three byte-identical replies.

mutations.name: K16 focus recall is re-served from the same frontier every call
mutations.find: .filter((i) => afterRecallMark({ ts: i.ts, id: i.id }, agent.recallCursor))
mutations.cell: successive calls walk the whole of focus recall instead of repeating its first window
mutations.expectRed: successive calls walk the whole of focus recall instead of repeating its first window
mutations.note: Reproduced by the second lens on a live broker: recall is re-derived from an unchanged frontier, so windowing its prefix returned the same fifteen of thirty messages three times while every reply promised a next batch. The window created that starvation, so the cursor is part of this change rather than a later one.

mutations.name: K17 the fresh filter compares timestamps only, so a tie is skipped
mutations.find: return a.ts !== b.ts ? a.ts > b.ts : a.id > b.id;
mutations.cell: a recall twin sharing a millisecond with a delivered item is not filtered out for good
mutations.expectRed: a recall twin sharing a millisecond with a delivered item is not filtered out for good
mutations.note: A timestamp is not a place in a queue when two items share it. Compare on time alone and the held twin is behind the mark forever, while the reply keeps promising a next batch: the starvation direction of the tie.

mutations.name: K18 the mark keeps the time and drops the id that breaks its ties
mutations.find: if (last) agent.noteRecalled({ ts: last.ts, id: last.id });
mutations.cell: ...and the twin already delivered is not re-served to pay for it
mutations.expectRed: ...and the twin already delivered is not re-served to pay for it
mutations.note: The other direction of the same tie: a mark that forgets which item it stopped at leaves the delivered twin ahead of it, so the next call serves it again. Starvation and repetition are the two ways a tie can be got wrong, and the cell asserts against both.

mutations.name: K19 the ordered lane steps over its own gap to fit later items
mutations.cell: ...and nothing behind the hole was re-served to get there
mutations.expectRed: ...and nothing behind the hole was re-served to get there
mutations.note: Stepping over a gap looks like better packing: the window is fuller and nothing is lost yet. But a lane walked by one mark cannot record a hole, so everything delivered past it is served again on the next call, forever. The free lane may step over its own gaps because each of its items is acked by id.
